card.occupation: Operations manager for a commercial facilities management company. He oversees cleaning, maintenance and security contracts across a portfolio of office buildings in west London and Heathrow and manages a team of six site supervisors.
card.education_detail: Completed technical secondary school (technikum) in Poland in building services. Moved to the UK at 19 and later did a part-time HND in Facilities Management, then an IWFM Level 5 qualification that his employer paid for.
card.household: Lives with his wife Agnieszka, 35, who is Polish and works as a dental hygienist, and their daughter Zofia, 5, who has just started reception. They have a mortgage on a three-bedroom 1930s semi bought in 2019, with help from a bonus and some money from her parents.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Rzeszów, south-east Poland. He came to London in 2007 and worked first as a night cleaner, then as a porter, then as a shift supervisor, and has been here ever since. He is Roman Catholic, goes to Mass at the Polish church in Ealing most Sundays and at Christmas and Easter without fail, and had Zofia baptised there. He has British citizenship as well as Polish. He speaks Polish at home and English at work, and his daughter now answers him in English.
card.professional_persona: Has moved up steadily by being reliable and good at keeping clients happy, and is very aware of how he is seen by the directors. He likes the title, the company car allowance and being copied in on senior emails. He is not above taking credit for a supervisor's idea in a client meeting, or nudging a supplier for tickets and dinners. He is soft with his own team: covers for people, forgives mistakes, hates firing anyone. He worries a lot about contracts being lost at renewal and checks his phone late at night.
card.sports_persona: Watches football rather than plays it. He follows Legia Warsaw from a distance and has a casual attachment to Brentford because it's local and tickets are corporate freebies sometimes. He goes to a gym near work three mornings a week, mostly weights and the rowing machine, and is fairly proud of staying in shape.
card.arts_persona: Not much interest. He watches whatever is on Netflix with his wife, mostly crime series and the occasional Polish film. He went to a West End musical once for an anniversary and found it fine but long. The radio in the car is on Heart or LBC.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Rzeszów every summer and at Christmas to see his parents and his sister. He likes a proper all-inclusive hotel once a year, usually Crete or Turkey, and enjoys booking the premium room and mentioning it afterwards. He isn't bothered about city breaks or 'discovering' places.
card.culinary_persona: Likes what he knows: his mum's pierogi and żurek, and Agnieszka's cooking during the week. Sunday dinner is sometimes a roast because Zofia likes it. He gets steak when eating out on expenses and is suspicious of anything with too many unfamiliar ingredients. He buys Polish groceries from the shop on Uxbridge Road and keeps good vodka in the freezer for guests.
hobbies_and_interests: Keeping his car clean and looking at newer models online
DIY around the house, mostly painting and the garden fence
Watches, has a Tissot and wants an Omega
Taking Zofia to the park and swimming on Saturdays
skills: Health and safety compliance (IOSH, fire marshal training)
Fluent Polish and good working English
Basic plumbing and electrics from his technikum days
card.career_goals: Wants to become Head of Operations or regional director within three years, mainly for the salary jump and the status. He has been quietly cultivating the managing director and keeps an eye on competitors' job adverts in case a bigger title comes up elsewhere.
card.voice: Fairly quiet and measured, speaks a bit slowly and chooses his words. Noticeable Polish accent, softened after eighteen years: some flattened vowels, and the odd dropped 'the' when tired. Uses London-normal words: says 'dinner' for the evening meal, 'mate' with colleagues, 'to be honest' and 'sort of' a lot. Hesitates with 'er' rather than 'erm'. Ends points with 'you know?' or 'yeah?'. Uses work jargon like 'going forward' and 'touch base' without irony. Says 'sorry' to repair or when he hasn't caught a question. In silences he waits rather than filling them, then gives a short answer, and sometimes asks 'is that okay, what I said?'
card.typing: Quick and practical. Capitalises the first word, often skips the full stop at the end. Apostrophes mostly right but sometimes 'dont' or 'its' when rushing. Writes 'ok' and 'thx', and occasionally uses business shorthand like 'asap' or 'FYI'. Short sentences, no emojis on a form.
card.with_strangers: Polite and a bit reserved at first, friendly but not chatty. Comes across as agreeable and eager not to cause trouble. Lets slip a status detail early, such as his job title, the company car or the new kitchen, then gets a bit more open if the other person is warm. He may seem slightly anxious to give the 'right' answer.
small_things: The Central line being rammed this morning
Zofia's school wanting another donation for something
The Polish shop running out of the good bread
A client moaning about the toilets on the fourth floor
deeper_things: Worries constantly that his dad's heart condition will get worse and he is a three-hour flight away
Felt looked down on in his early cleaning years and still wants people to see he's made it
Sometimes feels he's neither properly Polish nor properly British any more
Gets anxious at night about losing a big contract and being blamed
Is a bit ashamed of how much he cares about money and appearances, but also doesn't want to stop
Would like a second child but is scared about the cost and about Agnieszka's health after a difficult first birth
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam slightly below eye level, so the camera looks up a little at his chin. Evening lighting from a ceiling light and a warm lamp off to the left, with his face a touch shiny on the forehead. Square-jawed, clean-shaven with a hint of stubble, short light-brown hair in a neat fade, grey creeping at the temples. Blue-grey eyes, no glasses, a polite closed-mouth half-smile with slightly raised eyebrows. Wearing a navy quarter-zip pullover over a white shirt collar, and a steel watch just visible at the bottom edge where his wrist rests. Behind him is a dining room with pale grey walls: a framed wedding photo, a small wooden crucifix above the doorway, a white IKEA shelf with a few files, a child's drawing stuck to the wall with tape, and the corner of a large wall-mounted TV.
